title: Threshold-driven annotations and contrast-aware series highlight
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Goal: Design an annotations system that can: 1) render dynamic threshold-based annotation bands and point markers for time-series charts, 2) apply a contrast-aware series highlight mode for users with low-vision or high-contrast settings, and 3) degrade gracefully for very high-density data while minimizing layout and rendering cost.

Background: We currently show static annotations and simple tooltips. Customers building alerts and SLO dashboards need: visible thresholds (bands/markers), context-aware series emphasis when hovering or focusing, and an accessible alternative that meets WCAG contrast ratios for all token-driven palettes. Engineering has a parallel runtime change to expose annotation primitives and a draw-mode flag (canvas vs DOM).

Design requirements and proposed approach:
- Annotation patterns: two primary annotation types: (A) threshold band (continuous colored region with optional label) and (B) point marker with label and confidence indicator. Both types must support semantic ARIA labeling and be discoverable via keyboard navigation.
- Contrast-aware highlight: create a chart-level mode that toggles on user preference or forced by accessibility settings. When enabled, series emphasis uses contrast-boosted strokes and an adaptive fill that maintains tokenized color meaning but meets at least 4.5:1 contrast for text and 3:1 for adjacent fills where applicable.
- Token changes: add two new design tokens: --chart-annotation-band-opacity (default 0.12) and --chart-contrast-boost-factor (default 1.25). Update token documentation and include examples for primary/secondary palette mapping.
- Interaction model: keyboard focus lands on series legend item or a dedicated annotations layer toggle. Pressing Enter/Space focuses the first annotation; Tab cycles through annotations. Hover/focus on a series should apply highlight to only that series and de-emphasize others using a low-cost opacity reduction. Support short press vs long press gestures for touch to reveal annotation details.
- Performance considerations: prefer single-layer canvas compositing for high-density datasets; reserve DOM annotations for interactive/accessible contexts. Use lazy annotation rendering: annotations outside viewport or beyond current aggregation window should not be rendered until scrolled into view. Implement a debounced highlight state to avoid reflow during rapid mouse moves.

Accessibility and QA criteria:
- All interactive annotations must have accessible names via aria-label and a short description via aria-describedby.
- Keyboard-only users can reach annotations and read their labels and contextual time range.
- Contrast mode must pass automated color contrast checks for the most common palette combinations used in our dashboards.
- Reduced-motion: reveal/hide of bands and markers must respect prefer-reduced-motion and use instant opacity toggles rather than transitions when set.

Acceptance criteria (mockups/prototypes):
1) High-fidelity mockups for desktop and tablet: threshold band, point marker, legend-driven focus, and contrast mode examples.
2) Interactive prototype (Figma + embedded HTML/CSS) demonstrating keyboard traversal, focus states, and contrast toggle.
3) Token spec PR with updated tokens and migration notes.
4) Design handoff doc with accessibility checklist, microcopy for annotations, and performance guidance for runtime engineers.

Open questions and trade-offs:
- Should annotations be semantically present in the DOM even when rendering on canvas for assistive tech? (Trade-off: DOM presence improves accessibility but increases DOM size/cost.)
- How aggressive should contrast boosting be before we break brand color semantics? Need PM guidance on preserving color meaning versus accessibility priority.
- Touch UX: long-press discovery may be unfamiliar; consider a persistent toggle or legend affordance for mobile.

- Confluence spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CH/Annotation+Design+Spec (placeholder)

- Deliver Figma prototypes for accessibility testing by 2026-03-05.
- Pair with ENG-33221 to define the annotation primitive API and preferred default draw mode.
